name: McINTOSH, Melissa Iris

headline.note: American Express public-affairs work in September 2001 and undated Travelex communications work are now identified, but ordinary hours and employment boundaries remain unresolved. Australian Canoeing, university-centre, political-staff, nonprofit housing, party, study and elected roles are excluded. Wentworth resignation is documented on 7 December 2018. Private full-time years cannot be calculated from the remaining corporate and small-business evidence; missing evidence is not zero.

career_spells.employer: Western Sydney University (then University of Western Sydney)
career_spells.evidence_note: McIntosh's first speech says her political career began at age 21, fresh out of Western Sydney University. Secondary synthesis identifies a Bachelor of Communications covering journalism, public relations and video production, but enrolment and graduation dates are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Study is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Office of the Hon. Jackie Kelly MP
career_spells.evidence_note: In her first speech McIntosh calls Kelly her first political boss, says Kelly gave her a first job when she was fresh out of university and dates the start of her political career to age 21. The title, payroll, exact dates, hours and leave are not published in the reviewed sources.
career_spells.counting_note: Political-staff employment is displayed separately and excluded from the narrow headline.

career_spells.employer: Office of Prime Minister John Howard
career_spells.role: Press-office political staff member (exact title unresolved)
career_spells.evidence_note: McIntosh's first speech says she worked for Prime Minister Howard in Canberra at age 22 and served in his office. Exact title, payroll, appointment dates, hours, leave and the transition from Kelly's office are unresolved. Employer biography specifies the Press Office. Her later first-person account places Howard-office service approximately a year before September 2001, without establishing boundaries.
career_spells.counting_note: Political-staff employment is excluded from the narrow public/private headline.

career_spells.employer: American Express (Australian employing legal entity unresolved)
career_spells.role: Public affairs team member; exact title unresolved
career_spells.evidence_note: The previously unnamed Sydney corporate role is identified as American Express public affairs by her first-person September 2001 account and employer biography. Observed working there in September 2001; this is not a start/end date. The first speech describes subsequent family travel and a career pause, whose boundaries remain unknown. One crisis day with long hours does not prove substantive full-time status.
career_spells.counting_note: Private-sector employer identified; dates, ordinary hours and leave remain insufficient for a duration.

career_spells.role: Corporate communications and public affairs work; exact title unresolved
career_spells.evidence_note: Wentworth employer biography names Travelex among previous corporate communications/public-affairs employers. Sequence relative to American Express, appointment dates, pay, hours and leave unknown.

career_spells.employer: Unidentified small-business venture and travelling-with-kids website
career_spells.evidence_note: McIntosh's first speech describes a period in which she had her own small business and developed a travelling-with-kids website with Rebecca Collins. The legal entity, product, exact dates, ownership, revenue or pay, hours, leave and whether the activity was substantive employment are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Business activity may count only when substantive paid work and boundaries are supported; a founder narrative alone is insufficient.

career_spells.employer: Australian Canoeing Inc. (event payroll entity unconfirmed)
career_spells.evidence_note: Listed among professional staff at June 2005. This is an operational staff title, not the separately listed board of Australian Canoeing Events Limited. Exact payroll entity, start/end dates, pay, ordinary hours and leave unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Sporting association employment excluded; point-in-time staff listing is not a full-year interval.

career_spells.employer: United States Studies Centre, University of Sydney
career_spells.role: Director of W21 / Women in Leadership project, Head of Partnerships and Director of Events and Project Management
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen official extract supplies the combined roles and 2011–2015 range. McIntosh's first speech corroborates work at the Centre, says she started W21 there, and dates her International Dialogue on Women in Leadership to 2014. Exact appointment dates, title transitions, hours, leave and any overlap with other work are unresolved. A 29 October 2013 author footer identifies the Women in Leadership project title; the November 2014 event programme confirms W21 director. ABC supplies the fuller events/project-management title. These observations do not partition the 2011–2015 interval or prove full-time work.
career_spells.counting_note: University employment is kept distinct and excluded from the two narrow headline totals under the current codebook.

career_spells.employer: Office of the Hon. Alex Hawke MP, Assistant Minister to the Treasurer
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen official extract records Chief of Staff to Assistant Minister to the Treasurer Alex Hawke from 2015 to 2016. McIntosh's first speech confirms service in Hawke's office. Exact appointment and cessation dates, payroll, hours, leave and overlap with the USSC role are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Political-staff employment is excluded from the narrow public/private headline.

career_spells.evidence_note: Official start year remains 2016. The employer’s 2019 report explicitly gives resignation on 7 December 2018, resolving cessation. The 2017 report describes establishing the position that reporting year. Appointment day, ordinary hours, leave and overlap with campaigning still unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Nonprofit employment is excluded from the narrow public/private headline under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Liberal Party of Australia — NSW Division
career_spells.evidence_note: Secondary synthesis identifies these offices before federal election. Dates, remuneration and workload remain unknown. Removed election day as an unsupported cessation date.
career_spells.counting_note: Party organisational office is excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Liberal Party of Australia — NSW Division
career_spells.role: Candidate for Blue Mountains City Council, Fourth Ward
career_spells.evidence_note: Secondary synthesis, citing contemporary local reporting, records an unsuccessful Fourth Ward candidacy in 2016. Nomination and election dates, campaign remuneration, hours and overlap with the Hawke and Wentworth roles are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Candidacy and campaign activity are excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.employer: Liberal Party of Australia — NSW Division
career_spells.evidence_note: Public election accounts identify McIntosh as the Liberal candidate elected for Lindsay on 18 May 2019. The record uses only the published year for the campaign start; exact preselection and campaign dates, remuneration, hours and overlap with Wentworth Community Housing are unresolved.
career_spells.counting_note: Party candidacy and campaigning are excluded under the codebook.

career_spells.role: Member of the House of Representatives for Lindsay
career_spells.evidence_note: The frozen roster and current Parliament profile establish continuing House service for Lindsay from the 18 May 2019 election.
career_spells.counting_note: Federal elected office is excluded under the codebook.

research_notes: 2026-10-01 follow-up: corporate employer identified as American Express; added Travelex and Australian Canoeing staff roles. Employer annual report resolves Wentworth cessation. USSC contemporary title observations added; unsupported party-office election-day cessation removed.

Unresolved: exact dates, payroll, hours, leave and transitions across Kelly/Howard/Hawke offices, American Express, Travelex, canoeing and USSC; the duration and nature of the disclosed career pause; small-business name, website, ownership, remuneration and substantive working arrangements.

Searched name variants, employer annual reports, public professional and author profiles, contemporary USSC events and first-person September 2001 account. Corporate searches did not yield Travelex boundaries or full-time evidence. Canoeing staff table is June 2005 only; archived event-news indexing is not an employment interval.

Wentworth report text retrieved; initial PDF screenshots timed out. Canoeing PDF initially timed out on reopening, with indexed staff text and a later screenshot response available. These are individual-source retrieval errors, not job-wide blockers.

Follow up small-business website with Rebecca Collins, earlier/later canoeing annual reports and employment arrangements. Preserve unknown ordinary hours rather than infer full-time from executive titles, professional-staff classification or a single long crisis workday.
